source_of_truth: Read by hand from src/components/search/CountryPicker.tsx (React/Next .tsx, semantic engine). The custom combobox is a plain <div role="combobox" aria-expanded tabindex="0"> with no aria-label, no aria-labelledby and no associated visible label text: a real accessibility defect (a screen reader announces an unnamed combobox). But ui-audit judges only NATIVE HTML elements and does not model the accessible name of a custom ARIA widget, so this is a known coverage gap, declared in coverage_gaps[] and excluded from recall — not an FN of a rule the tool has. The native <input id="q"> is correctly associated with <label for="q">, so form-control-without-label must not fire on it. Truth derived from the source only; the tool was not consulted.
provenance: blind generalization: truth derived from source without consulting tool output

coverage_gaps.what: custom <div role="combobox"> with aria-expanded and tabindex but no accessible name (no aria-label / aria-labelledby / associated label); ui-audit's native-element scope does not cover custom-widget names

forbidden.why_not_a_defect: the native <input id="q"> is associated with <label for="q">, so it has a label.
